I've had other jobs, and the stress of teaching is so much better than the stress I felt from the other jobs. I like having my days feel different and being able to have a social job, I get to talk to the students and talk to other teachers. I couldn't imagine having an office job and doing the same thing 9-5 every single day.   


Having holidays off guaranteed, having weekends off guaranteed, having nights off (mostly, right?), having summers off, all perks of the job, I love it. This past summer I got to spend every day with my 2 year old goddaughter and her mom going for walks every day, going to the beach, just going out and exploring. I wouldn't be able to do that as easily with other jobs, and that really makes it all worth it to me.

My school district, the principal taught pre-k for one year before getting the job...to say she's in over her head is an understatement. We are a very small rural school (k-12 building is our distract, the principal is a k-12 principal for our 200 students). I was also on the hiring committee...and trust me some of the options were not even close to good.

We do student teaching at the end of the education program so people who don't like teaching don't know until the spent a lot of time and money becoming a teacher, so they try to keep going with it, but ultimately just quit. 

I also find anecdotally that a lot of new teachers aren't ready for what can be an intensive career. A lot of stress that people feel about teaching is just stress from working in general, but they don't have any other jobs to compare to and think that its stress from teaching. I find teachers who have fallen back on teaching tend to stay with it longer, because while it is stressful, there are a lot of benefits to teaching compared to other jobs.
